name: Docusate sodium (Docusol)
mechanism: Anionic surfactant - reduces surface tension of stool, allowing water and fats to penetrate, softening hard faeces. Stimulates fluid secretion in small/large intestine (mild)
dosing: Adults: 200-500mg daily in divided doses (usually 100mg BD-TDS). Up to 500mg daily. Children >12y: 100-300mg daily. Take with plenty of fluids. Oral capsules or liquid. Onset: 1-3 days. May take with food
contraindications: Intestinal obstruction, acute abdominal conditions (appendicitis, undiagnosed abdominal pain), nausea/vomiting, severe dehydration. Caution: hepatic impairment (sodium docusate absorbed)
interactions: May increase absorption of other drugs (surfactant effect). Liquid paraffin (↑ absorption of paraffin - avoid combination). Danthron (may ↑ liver toxicity). Aspirin (theoretical ↑ GI irritation)
monitoring: Bowel movement frequency and consistency. Hydration status. Signs of electrolyte imbalance with prolonged use. Abdominal pain or distension (may indicate obstruction)
pregnancy: Generally considered safe - poorly absorbed systemically. Widely used in pregnancy. Avoid high doses. Adequate fluid intake essential. Lactulose often preferred as first-line
sideEffects: Common: abdominal cramps, diarrhoea (excessive dose), nausea, bitter taste (liquid). Uncommon: rash, throat irritation (liquid). Rare: hepatotoxicity with chronic high-dose use (case reports)
pharmacokinetics: Oral administration. Some systemic absorption (undergoes enterohepatic circulation). Absorbed fraction metabolized in liver. Most excreted in faeces. Onset: 1-3 days for stool softening effect
clinicalPearls: Often combined with stimulant laxatives (senna, bisacodyl) in compound preparations (e.g., co-danthramer, co-danthrusate - restricted to palliative care due to carcinogenicity concerns). Mild effect compared to osmotic laxatives (macrogol, lactulose). Most useful for preventing hard stools (e.g., post-MI, haemorrhoids, anal fissure, post-operative, with opioids). Not first-line for chronic constipation - bulk-forming or osmotic laxatives preferred. Ensure adequate fluid intake (6-8 glasses/day) or may worsen constipation. Less effective if already severely constipated - may need stimulant laxative initially. Available OTC. Liquid formulation can be mixed with juice/milk to improve taste. If no effect after 5 days, consider alternative laxative or investigate cause
indication: Constipation (particularly hard stools), prevention of constipation in patients at risk (cardiac conditions, haemorrhoids, anal fissure, after rectal surgery), adjunct with opioid therapy
